findings.title: No optimistic concurrency guard on the state-scoped delete
findings.description: The DELETE on COMPANY is filtered by ID (primary key) and COMPANY_STATE but carries no version or last-updated-time predicate. Between a prior read and this delete, a concurrent update can modify the row while leaving COMPANY_STATE unchanged, so the delete removes a row whose post-update contents were never observed by the caller (lost-update window); conversely, if COMPANY_STATE changed concurrently, the delete affects zero rows, which the caller silently misses unless it checks the affected-row count. Static observation only; unverified at runtime. No native Database MCP call was made (static-review-only statement).
findings.recommendation: Have the mapper return the affected-row count and treat rows == 0 as 'row not found or state changed'. If concurrent state changes are possible, add an optimistic-lock predicate (e.g., a VERSION column or UPDATE_TIME) to the WHERE clause, and ensure the caller wraps this delete and related writes in a single transaction.

findings.title: Transaction and affected-row handling are delegated to the caller
findings.description: The mapper XML declares no transaction semantics for this delete; commit, rollback, and error handling live outside the statement. A caller that ignores the returned count can silently assume deletion succeeded even when the state guard prevented it. Static observation only; unverified at runtime.
findings.recommendation: Document that the mapper method returns the affected-row count (int) and that callers must manage transactions explicitly and react to rows == 0. Consider replacing parameterType java.util.Map with a typed parameter object or @Param-annotated method arguments so binding keys are verified at compile time, and add a DAO-level test asserting the guarded delete affects zero rows when COMPANY_STATE mismatches.
